facts.text: CausalWorld subclasses gym.Env, the legacy OpenAI Gym environment API
With visualization disabled the structured observation mode uses an in-process PyBullet client connected with pybullet.DIRECT
The documented use constructs the environment as CausalWorld(task=task, enable_visualization=True)
The constructor defaults to structured observations, joint_positions actions and normalized actions and observations
One environment step multiplies a 1/250 s simulation step by skip_frame
skip_frame defaults to 10
The reaching task's default episode length is 5 seconds
The constructor converts the task's default episode length to int(length / dt)
The joint-position action bounds are [-1.57, -1.2, -3.0] repeated for three fingers to [1.0, 1.57, 3.0] repeated
When actions are normalized the action space is Box(low=-1, high=1), one element per joint-position bound
The reaching task's robot observation keys are time_left_for_task, joint_positions, joint_velocities and end_effector_positions
The reaching task's stage observation keys are the three goal cartesian positions
A goal silhouette's cartesian position is bounded from [-0.5, -0.5, 0] to [0.5, 0.5, 0.5]
The structured observation space concatenates the robot and stage spaces into one Box
Normalized observations use the bounds -1 and 1
A step returns observation, reward, done and info, and scales the reward by dt
reset takes no seed and returns the task's structured observation
seed reseeds gym's np_random and numpy and returns the seed in a list
An episode is done when the episode length is greater than the maximum episode length
The info dictionary carries desired_goal, achieved_goal, success and fractional_success
The environment exposes get_state and set_state for pybullet_state and control_index
close saves an attached data recorder and closes the robot
The reaching task's default goals are [0, 0, 0.10], [0, 0, 0.13] and [0, 0, 0.16]

determinism.notes: the fake draws the start joints from Python's random.Random seeded by the bridge and has no other randomness; upstream seeds numpy (causalworld.py:342-343) and was not run, so one seed does not reproduce upstream's trajectory

gaps: the checked fake is a kinematic stand-in: joint positions are set directly, with no PyBullet rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, PD controller, actuator, sensor or noise model; the upstream is a PyBullet TriFinger simulation (causalworld.py:962-967) and was never compared with the fake
the fake models only the default reaching task with structured observations; the other task generators, pixel camera observations, interventions and the real TriFinger are not modelled
the fake draws the initial joint offsets from Python's random.Random while upstream seeds numpy (causalworld.py:342-343), so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and only cap.world.step.v1 advances simulated time; one 40 ms control step stands for 10 PyBullet substeps of 4 ms (causalworld.py:93-96)

snapshot and restore are not offered by this package even though the upstream class has get_state and set_state (causalworld.py:492-521); the fake does not implement them, so determinism is declared seeded rather than exact

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: the runtime latch refuses step and reset after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears it, and the fake keeps its state readable
